about: Evaluation questions with expected answers. Each ticket case is the exact New ticket form input; each KB case is the exact KB Assistant question. Type them into the app and you see the expected result. Run all of them with: python -m build.run_eval_cases
how_expected_was_decided: Held-out tickets (INC-xxxxx from the 15% test split, never trained on and not in the search index): labels = the dataset's true labels, outcome = the decision table in src/decide.py applied to those labels. Probes (hand-written): labels from the rules in src/rules.py worked out by hand. Expected KB article chosen by reading the article titles. Only the fields listed under 'expected' are checked. 'expected' is always the RIGHT answer; where the app is known to show something else on one field, 'known_misses' says what it shows and why (reported separately, not counted as a failure).

fields.outcome: banner at the top of the result: RECOMMEND / REVIEW / ESCALATE / NEED_INFO
fields.category, subcategory, symptom_type, pri: the four cards under the banner
fields.escalate_to: '-> hand to ...' line in the banner (ESCALATE only, else null)
fields.hype_detected: violet chip 'Hype detected - ignored for priority'
fields.user_agrees: false = orange chip 'You chose X - model says Y'
fields.knowledge_gap: grey chip 'Knowledge gap' + warning on the KB articles tab
fields.possible_duplicate: red chip 'Possible duplicate of a past ticket'
fields.top_similar: first card on the Similar past tickets tab
fields.top_kb: first card on the KB articles tab
fields.fix_from: KB article the Recommended fix tab is written from (a list = any of these is fine; null = no fix shown)
fields.reasons_contains: text that must appear in the banner's reason lines
fields.priority_reason_contains: text that must appear in the sentence on the Priority card
fields.masked_description_contains / _excludes: Audit record tab: what the stored description must / must not contain
fields.answered: KB Assistant: true = numbered steps, false = 'I couldn't find this in the knowledge base' + ticket summary
fields.answer_from: KB Assistant: KB article the steps cite
fields.cites_only_self_help: KB Assistant: every citation badge is a KB-xxx/self/n step (employees never see support steps)
fields.only_public_sources: KB Assistant: no internal article is ever listed
fields.source_ids_excludes: KB Assistant: these articles must not appear under 'Sources'

tickets.title: App example 'VPN on, shared drive off'
tickets.tests: happy path: everything agrees -> confident cited fix
tickets.why: VPN is a critical service; 'drive will not open' = blocked -> impact Medium. Environment is not Production -> urgency Medium. Medium x Medium = P3. KB-020 is written for exactly this problem.

input.description: My VPN says connected but the shared drive will not open from home.

tickets.title: T01 + the 'URGENT - I'm the CEO' hype toggle
tickets.tests: hype changes nothing except the hype chip
tickets.why: Priority comes from service, environment, who is affected and symptom only. Same facts as T01 -> same answer, plus the hype flag.

input.description: URGENT — I'm the CEO, fix this now! My VPN says connected but the shared drive will not open from home.

tickets.title: App example 'INC-00347 - hype + wrong guess' (held out)
tickets.tests: hype ignored, wrong user category corrected, P2 from facts -> escalate with the fix attached
tickets.why: True labels: Business System > Error or won't open, blocked, Applications, P2 (just me on a critical service = Medium impact; blocked in Production = High urgency). P2 -> ESCALATE. KB-030 is the only Payroll 'won't open' article.

input.description: I'm getting heat from above. Please pick this up immediately. My workng salary application closes just after login. I can see the menu for a moment but can't open a run.

tickets.title: App example 'Calm vs hype (printer)'
tickets.tests: a covered service but an uncovered problem: faint printing has no KB article -> no invented fix
tickets.why: Device & Software > Printer problem; there is a workaround ('alternate device') -> slow; my team -> impact Medium, slow -> urgency Medium = P3. The three printer articles are about a paused queue, badge release and paper size; none is about faint print, so the LLM must refuse and it becomes a knowledge gap -> ESCALATE to Desktop Support.

input.description: Printed handover sheets are too faint for my team on the regular printer. We're selecting the alternate device and can get the forms out.

known_misses.symptom_type: The app shows 'blocked'. The data spec says a workaround means 'slow', so 'slow' is the right answer and this is a model miss. It is harmless here: my team + not Production gives P3 either way.

tickets.title: T04 + the hype toggle
tickets.tests: hype changes nothing except the hype chip
tickets.why: Same facts as T04 -> same answer, plus the hype flag.

input.description: URGENT — I'm the CEO, fix this now! Printed handover sheets are too faint for my team on the regular printer. We're selecting the alternate device and can get the forms out.

known_misses.symptom_type: Same model miss as T04: the app shows 'blocked'; the right answer is 'slow'. Priority is P3 either way.

tickets.title: App example 'Vague ticket'
tickets.tests: completeness check: too vague -> questions, no fix
tickets.why: Every word is generic ('system', 'not', 'working'), so the completeness check fires before any fix is attempted. Rule 1 of the decision table -> NEED_INFO with the two default questions.

input.description: system not working

questions: Which application, device or service is affected?
What exactly happens, and is there an error message?

tickets.title: Probe: personal data in the description
tickets.tests: PII is masked before search, the LLM and the audit log; the ticket is still solved
tickets.why: The email address and phone number must be replaced by [email] and [phone]. The problem itself: desktop email keeps asking for the password while webmail works (a workaround = slow) -> Email & Communication > Email problem, Applications, P4. KB-010 is exactly this. Outcome is REVIEW, not RECOMMEND: 'keeps asking for my password' reads like credential phishing, so P(Security) = 0.32, above the 0.20 safety-net threshold -> 'possible security issue' -> a human glances at it. That is the designed trade-off (a false alarm costs a minute; a missed phishing case costs much more). Masking is not the cause: P(Security) is the same without the contact details.

input.description: The email app on my laptop keeps asking for my password. Webmail still works, so I can read mail there. Reach me at jo.bloggs@example.com or +44 7700 900123.
